identify.intro: US-delivered trucks, Colombian imports, Japanese fire trucks and Indian Jongas all look alike, and many US 60s for sale today are recent imports. Know which one you're looking at.

items.head: US-market trucks
items.body: Restorer SNLC says the US got short-wheelbase L60 soft-tops and KL60 hardtops, all with a three-speed and a C216 rear axle. A BaT US-market 1965 had chassis 4-L60-02697 and an 80-mph speedometer.

items.head: Imports
items.body: Colombian trucks on BaT show km/h speedometers and chassis numbers such as L60…, KL60… and, on 1980–82 LG-61 trucks, G61…, with four-speed gearboxes. Ask for the import paperwork.

items.head: Front axle joints
items.body: SNLC says early front axles (before about 1968) use Tracta joints and later ones Birfields.

items.head: Speedometer drive
items.body: Pre-1966 trucks drive the speedometer from the front of the transfer case; later trucks have a splined pinion behind the 4WD flange.

items.head: Fire Patrols
items.body: Wikipedia says the two-wheel-drive Fire Patrol lacks the 4x4 badge, transfer lever and front differential, but every Fire Patrol has a PTO lever for the pump.

values.intro: Refurbished Colombian imports bring the most money in the US. The original US-delivered trucks that come up tend to be rougher and cheaper.
values.note: Based on 10 Bring a Trailer sales of 60-series trucks (including 1980–82 Colombian LG-61s) from February 2025 to July 2026. Top sale: a refurbished ex-Colombia 1965 at $23,000 (2026).

paragraphs: Nissan sold the 60 new in the US only from 1962 to 1969, so many trucks for sale today are imports, especially from Colombia. Every 60 is well past the 25-year mark, so NHTSA's exemption from federal safety standards applies, counted from the date of manufacture.
State titling and emissions rules still apply. Several recent BaT imports were titled in Florida. Make sure the chassis number matches the import documents.

production.intro: Nissan built the 60 in Japan for twenty years, and it was assembled or derived in India and kept alive in Colombia.
